NO.4157/2010, being aggrieved by the Judgment of his conviction and sentence dated 01.01.2013 passed in the said criminal case for the offence punishable under Section 392 read with Section 34 of IPC, sentencing him to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for two years and pay fine of Rs.2,000/- with default sentence and this Judgment of conviction and sentence being affirmed by the learned Fast Track Court, Bhadravathi in Crl.A. No.11/2013 by Judgment dated 06.08.2014, has preferred this Revision petition.

2. The said criminal case was registered based upon the charge-sheet being filed by the New Town Police Station, Bhadravathi, based upon a complaint filed by the complainant by name Smt. Indira Murthy, wife of L. Ramamurthy, at 9.45 p.m. on 11.08.2010 alleging that, she is the resident of the address so stated in the complaint. Her husband is a retired person from VISL and was suffering from pain in his hands. Therefore, on 11.10.2010, herself and her husband had been to VISL Hospital Colony and were returning to their house at 6.30 p.m. by walk on the pathway situated behind New Colony, Karimaremma Temple. By the side of the said pathway, shrubs were grown. Her husband was moving ahead and complainant was following him. At that time, two persons were found on the said pathway and one person was found parked a cement colour scooter and was standing there and when her husband went ahead, other person came to the complainant, threatened her, put his hand on her neck. She fell down. She gave the chain worn by her in neck valuing about Rs.40,000/-. It was containing black beeds (karimani) and it is a golden wedlock chain containing one havala. The said gold ornament was of 'V' shape. 4 The said persons were well built and one person was wearing black 'T' shirt and one person was wearing jeans pant. Her husband chased the said person who snatched the chain. But the said person leaving the chappals and scooter, ran away. Complainant was afraid. Thereafter, went to her house and at 9.45 p.m. went to the New Town Police Station and lodged the complaint before P.W.8 - Shivanna, the then Head Constable of New Town Police Station.
3. This P.W.8 on receipt of the complaint, registered the same in Crime No.121/2010, prepared the F.I.R. as per Ex.P8 and set the criminal law in motion.

4. P.W. 7 - Yogeshwarappa, being the Head Constable of the said Police Station, along with his other police staff were deputed for tracing the accused persons. Accordingly on 16.08.2010, P.W. 8 and C.W. 10 to 12 were doing day patrolling duty at various places from 8.a.m. onwards. At 10.00 a.m., when they went to Bhandarahalli and were watching near the Masjid, at that time, two persons were found standing near a shop. On seeing the police, they tried to run away from the said place. 5 But P.W.7 and his staff chased them and caught hold them. By apprehending them, produced both accused persons at 10.45 a.m. before P.W.9 - H.S. Raju, the then Sub-Inspector of New Town Police Station.

5. This P.W.9 after production of accused before him, arrested them, recorded their voluntary statement as per Exs.P10 and P11. During the course of their voluntary statement, both the accused confessed about crime at various places and stated that if the police accompany them, they will produce the ornaments being subject matter of robbery. Accordingly, P.W.9 collected panchas and these accused led the police to the place where they had concealed the gold ornaments.

6. This P.W.9 in the presence of panchas, seized the said gold ornaments under Ex.P5. Called the complainant to the police station, showed the said gold ornaments. Recorded her statement. He also seized the scooter, chappal etc. The said articles seized by P.W.9 are marked as M.O. Nos. 1 to 4. 6
7. This P.W.9 produced accused Nos.1 and 2 before the Court and they were remanded to judicial custody. Thereafter, they were enlarged on bail.
8. New Town Police after completion of the investigation filed the charge-sheet against accused persons for the offence under Section 384 read with Section 34 of IPC.

9. The learned Civil Judge and Addl. JMFC, after filing of charge-sheet, took cognizance. Copies of the police papers were furnished to the accused persons as contemplated under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

10. After hearing both the sides, the learned Trial Court framed charge against accused persons for the offence punishable under Section 392 read with Section 34 of IPC and read over the same to the accused. They pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
11. To prove the guilt of the accused, prosecution in all examined nine witnesses from P.W.1 to P.W.9 and got marked 7 Exs.P1 to P10, so also M.O. Nos.1 to 4. Closed prosecution evidence.

12. After closure of the prosecution side evidence, accused Nos.1 and 2 were questioned under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. so as to enable them to answer the incriminating circumstances appearing in the evidence of the prosecution. They denied their complicity in the crime and did not choose to lead any defence evidence on their behalf.
13. Having heard the arguments from both the sides, the learned Trial Court found both the accused guilty of the offence under Section 392 read with Section 34 of IPC and sentenced them as aforesaid.

14. Being aggrieved by the same, it is accused No.1 preferred Crl.A. No.11/2013 before the Fast track Court, Bhadravathi. The learned Presiding Officer of Fast Track Court, Bhadravathi, after securing the Trial Court records and hearing arguments, affirmed the Judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the Trial Court vide Judgment dated 06.08.2014. This is how now 8 accused No.1 - Revision Petitioner is before this Court challenging the said Judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the Trial Court and confirmed by the First Appellate Court, on the following grounds:

15. That the conviction and sentence passed by both the Courts are contrary to law and evidence on record and probabilities of the case. Both the Courts have not considered the facts and circumstances of the case in proper perspective and hence the Judgments so passed by both the Courts are illegal, capricious and opposed to the sound principles of law.

16. A grave error has been committed by both the Courts in appreciating the evidence of interested testimony of P.W.1, P.W.2 and P.W.3. Both the Courts have committed error in appreciating the evidence of these witnesses as there is no corroborative evidence adduced by the prosecution. There is no proper analysis of the evidence. No identification parade was conducted so as to identify the accused persons. Recovery is not proved in accordance with law. Cross-examination of P.Ws. 1 to 3 is not properly appreciated. Both the Court have failed to take 9 note of hostility of P.W.4 and 5 and would have acquitted the revision petitioner - accused No.1. The evidence so recorded would have been discarded by both the Courts. As there is a serious error committed by both the Courts which has resulted in miscarriage of justice. Benefit of provisions of section 3 and 4 of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958, would have been given to the accused. A harsh and disproportionate sentence is imposed against accused. Hence, amongst other grounds, it is prayed to allow this revision petition and acquit the revision petitioner - accused No.1.

17. After filing this revision petition, revision petitioner was granted bail. Learned High Court Government Pleader took notice of this revision petition. Records of the Trial Court and First Appellate Court are secured.
18. I have heard the arguments of learned Advocate for the revision petitioner and learned HCGP. Meticulously perused the records.

19. It is submitted by the Advocate for the petitioner that both Trial Court and Appellate Court have committed grave error in appreciating the evidence being placed on record by the prosecution. It is submitted that, the very identification of the accused is disputed in this case. No proper procedure is being followed by the Investigating Agency in getting identification of the accused persons. It is a serious lacuna in the case of prosecution. It is further submitted that but even then, the learned Trial Court and the Appellate Court have misconstrued the facts brought on record and in view of the grounds so stated in the Revision Petition, he is entitled for acquittal.

20. As against this submission, the learned HCGP supported the reasons being assigned by the Trial Court and First Appellate Court and also submits that findings thereon are the factual findings with sound reasons and he supported the reasons and findings of both the Courts. It is prayed to dismiss the Revision Petition.
21. In the light of the submissions made by both the Advocates and the evidence placed on record, the following point arises for my consideration:
" 1. Whether the learned Trial Court and the Appellate Court have committed any legal error in arriving at the conclusion of finding guilty of petitioner No.1?"
22. To ascertain the same, we have to read both oral and documentary evidence produced, coupled with the position of law.

23. In this case, as discussed by the Trial Court and Appellate Court, P.W.4 - Francis being pancha to Ex.P2 - spot panchanama, so also P.W.5 - Salman Raj have been turned hostile. So also P.W.6 - Yogesh pancha to Ex.P5 - seizure panchanama has been turned hostile. Therefore the learned Trial Court and the Appellate Court have held that the evidence of these three witnesses would not come to the rescue of the prosecution. When the said witnesses have turned hostile, as rightly submitted by the learned Advocate for the Revision 12 Petitioner, no evidentiary value can be attached to the evidence of these witnesses.

24. P.W.1 being the complainant and P.W.2 being her husband, in their respective examination-in-chief have spoken to before the Court on oath, that on 11.08.2010, after consulting the doctor at VISL Hospital at about 6.30 p.m., they were returning to their house on the pathway situated behind the Karimaremma Temple by the side of the said hospital. At that time, they noticed two persons standing with a scooter by parking the same on the road. P.W.2 was moving ahead and P.W.1 was following him. At that time, amongst said two persons, one person caught hold of neck of P.W.1 - Indramma, threatened her and gave a threat to her to remove her wedlock chain, otherwise, he will strangulate her. By saying so, he caught hold of her neck. P.W.1 scared and as she was put under threat, she removed the said golden wedlock and gave it to accused No.1. She shouted. When her husband chased, one person tried to assault him with stone. Another person tried to start the scooter, but he could not. Therefore, leaving the said 13 scooter and chappal, they ran away with the golden wedlock. Before the Court on oath, P.W.1 identifies the persons as the persons who committed robbery of her golden wedlock. She identifies M.O. Nos.1 to 4 being the wedlock, chappal scooter. She further deposes that after two days, she was called by the Station and there she was shown with M.Os.1 to 4.
25. Though this P.W.1 has been directed with severe and searching cross-examination, but she has withstood the test of cross-examination.

26. Likewise, P.W.2 corroborates the evidence of P.W.1 in material particulars and he too identifies both accused as well as M.O. Nos.1 to 4. The other aspects in the cross-examination with regard to opening of the hospital, its working hours etc. have been brought on record. Though he too has been cross- examined at length, he also has withstood the test of cross- examination.

27. P.W.7 being the police official, has stated that, he was deputed by his superior officer along with other police staff 14 shown as C.W.10 to C.W.12 to trace the accused in Crime No.121/2010. Accordingly, on 16.08.2010, they were doing day patrolling duty and when they came near Masjid at Bhandarahalli, they noticed the two persons i.e. accused Nos.1 and 2 were standing in front of a shop. On seeing the police, they tried to run away. But, accused Nos.1 and 2 were chased and they were caught hold by P.W.7 and his staff and thereafter, they were produced before P.W.9.
28. Though this P.W.7 has been cross-examined by the defence, but nothing worth is elicited in the cross-examination so as to disbelieve his version given in the examination-in chief.

29. P.W.8 being SHO on 11.08.2010 received the complaint, registered the same, prepared the FIR and set the criminal law in motion. Except the denial in cross-examination, nothing is brought on record from the mouth of this P.W.8. Thus, immediately after the incident, a complaint was filed by the complainant. This fact is not denied by the defence. 15

30. P.W.9 is the I.O. in this case. He states that this P.W.7 along with other police staff produced both the accused before him on 16.08.2010 and he arrested them. When he interrogated them, they gave voluntary statement admitting about the commission of offence and also stated that if the police accompany them, they will show about the concealment of the articles being the subject matter of robbery. Accordingly, he collected the panchas and went along with the accused persons to the place where accused No.1 took them. It is accused No.1 took the police to his house, produced the Bajaj Scooter two ear ornaments, one golden ring, golden wedlock and other articles. He prepared the panchanama regarding recovery of said M.O. Nos. 1 to 4 under Ex.P5.

31. Though this P.W.9 has been thoroughly cross-examined, except the denial, nothing is elicited from the mouth of this witness. In all criminal cases, police officials are the supervisors of the investigation and panchas are the authors of the panchanama.

32. P.W.3 Thippeswamy is pancha to Ex.P5. He deposes before the Court with regard to seizure of said M.Os. at the instance of accused No.1. He identifies them having been photographed as per Ex.P4. Though this P.W.3 has been directed with lengthy cross-examination, but he has withstood the test of cross- examination. When there is a lengthy cross-examination, some minor contradictions, omissions are bound to occur. Though it is pointed out by the learned Advocate for the Revision Petitioner that there are contradictions, omissions, etc. but they will not shake the very basic case of the prosecution. P.Ws.1 and 2 have clearly identified these accused persons who have committed the offence of robbery. The said offence has taken place at about 6.30 p.m. on 11.08.2020. At that time, as per the say of P.W.1 and P.W.2, still there was light. So they could identify these accused persons both at the scene of occurrence and as well as when they were examined before the Court. So when there is a clear identification of accused Nos.1 and 2 by these eye witnesses being the victims, the argument that there was no identification parade cannot be accepted. Therefore, there is no substance in the submission of learned counsel for the accused. 17

33. In this case, the offence of robbery is attributed against accused persons. Robbery is a special and aggravated form of either theft or extortion and in every robbery, all the elements of either theft or extortion must be existent. In extortion - robbery, there must be a threatened injury. In this case, P.W.1 has categorically stated that accused No.1 gave a threat, caught hold of her neck and threatened her with dire consequences of life. So this conduct of accused No.1 attracts the ingredients of Section 392 of IPC.

34. The complaint and FIR do disclose the description of the accused persons and they have been identified by P.W.1 and P.W.2 when they are examined on oath before the Court. More so, there is a recovery of these M.Os. at the instance of accused persons. When there is a recovery and possession of stolen property, then, the presumption is permitted under Section 114 Illustration A of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. Therefore, if the gold ornaments which were found in possession of the accused and recovered from him as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in TULSIRAM KANU VS. STATE reported in AIR 1954 18 SC 1, a presumption of guilt may be permitted. No fixed time limit can be laid down to determine possession is recent or otherwise. Each case must be judged on its own facts. The question as to what amounts to recent possession sufficient to justify the presumption of guilt varies accordingly "as the stolen article are/is not calculated to pass readily from hand to hand". In this case, immediately within few days of lodging a complaint, the said gold ornaments with other articles are recovered as per the disclosure statements made by the accused persons when they were apprehended by the police. The learned Trial Court was justified in holding that the disclosure statements of the accused persons and recoveries from them at their instance by itself was sufficient circumstance which clearly show that the accused persons had joined hands to commit the offence of robbery. Therefore, recent and unexplained possession of stolen properties will be taken to be presumptions under the provisions of Indian Evidence Act . The best evidence has been placed on record by the prosecution to connect the accused persons with the offence of robbery because there is no proper explanation or account for the possession of these articles by accused persons. 19 Therefore, there are no valid and acceptable grounds mentioned in the Revision Petition so as to interfere into the concurrent findings of both the Courts, finding the accused persons guilty of the offence under Section 392 read with Section 34 of IPC.

35. Imposition of sentence without considering its effect on the social order in many cases may be in reality a futile exercise. The social impact of the crime for example where it leads to offences against women like the case on hand of committing robbery of gold ornaments worn by her which have great impact and serious repercussions on social order and public interest, cannot be lost sight of and per se require exemplary treatment. Any liberal attitude by imposing major sentences or taking two sympathetic views merely on account of lapse of time or considerations pursuant to the accused only in respect of such offences will be result-wise counter-productive in the long run and against social interest which need to be cared for and strengthened by the required string of deterrence inbuilt in the sentencing system. So to say, when such robbery is committed, deterrent punishment is called for.

36. It is submitted that Revision Petitioner - accused No.1 is a young person and has to take care of his family. This case is of the year 2010. In view of passage of time for a period of more than a decade, some leniency is to be shown in imposing sentence as there are no circumstances to invoke the provisions of Probation of Offenders Act . Therefore, to some extent, the sentence of imprisonment so imposed is to be modified and Revision Petitioner - accused No.1 if sentenced to undergo R.I. for one year, it would meet the ends of justice. So far as other sentence so imposed is concerned, it is to be maintained.

37. It is held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in a Judgment reported in (2008) 14 SCC 457 in SOUTHERN SALES AND SERVICES AND OTHERS VS. SAUERMILCH DESIGN AND HANDLES GmbH , it is well established principle of law that, the Revisional Court will not interfere even if a wrong order is passed by a Court having jurisdiction, in the absence of a jurisdictional error.

38. It is well settled that in exercise of revisional jurisdiction under Section 397 of code of Criminal procedure, the High Court does not, in the absence of perversity, upset concurrent factual findings. It is not for the Revisional Court to re-analyse and re- interpret the evidence on record. That means, interference by the High Court in exercise of revisional jurisdiction is limited to the exceptional cases, viz., (i) When it is found that order under revision suffers from glaring illegality or has caused miscarriage of justice, (2) When it is found that Trial Court has no jurisdiction to try the case. (3) When Trial Court has illegally shut out the evidence which otherwise ought to have been considered and (4) Where material evidence which clinches the issue has been overlooked.

39. It is held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in STATE OF GUJARAT VS AFROZ MOHAMMAD HASANFATTA, reported in 2019 CRL. L.J. 3366, 338(SC) that "while hearing revision under section 397 of Cr.P.C., the High court does not sit as an Appellate Court and will not re-appreciate the evidence unless the judgment of the trial court suffers from perversity". 22

40. As the learned Trial Court and the Appellate Court have rightly appreciated the facts of the case and the findings of the Trial Court and the Appellate Court are based upon the facts and law, being a Revisional Court, this Court cannot sit as an Appellate Court and re-appreciate the evidence.

41. In view of my foregoing discussions and the reasons stated thereon, the revision petition fails and is liable to be dismissed. Accordingly, I record my finding on point No.1 in the negative and resultantly pass the following:
ORDER The Revision Petition filed by the Petitioner - Accused No.1 is dismissed.
The Judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the Trial Court in C.C. No. 4157/2010 dated 01.01.2013 and the Appellate Court in Crl. A. No.11/2013 dated 06.08.2014 are hereby confirmed.
However, there shall be modification of the sentence in the following terms:

Accused No.1 shall undergo R.I. for one year. Set off is given under Section 428 of Cr.P.C. Accused No.1 shall surrender before the Trial Court forthwith to undergo the balance sentence. So far as other sentence is concerned, it is maintained.
Intimate the Trial Court and the Appellate Court regarding modification of the sentence, forthwith.
Send back the Trial Court and Appellate Court records.

case_name: Siddesh Pappanna v. State By Town Police

paragraphs.text: This revision is directed against the judgment of conviction passed against the accused-revision petitioner in C.C.No.614/2011 on the file of Prl. Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Chikkamagalur, dated 18.11.2013 registered for the offences punishable under Section 392 of IPC which is confirmed by the Prl. Sessions Judge, Chikkamagalur, in Crl.A.No.418/2013 dated 09.01.2015.
2. The parties to this revision are referred to as per their ranks before the trial Court for the purpose of convenience.

3. That one Dr. C.K.Uma lodged a complaint on 18.05.2011 at 9 p.m. by appearing before the Sub- Inspector of Chikkamagalur town police station, stating that she is a Gynecologist by profession. On 18.05.2011 during evening hours at about 7.35 p.m., she went to emergency ward of District Government Hospital of Chikkamagalur, to attend the patient. When she was returning towards her residential quarters along with her sister Annapurna inside the compound wall of the -3- CRL.RP.NO.701/2015 residential quarters near the residential quarters of Shalini and Gracy being the nurses, one stranger came from behind aged in between 25 and 30 years and snatched the gold chain worn by her weighing 14.800 grams. She bombarded. By hearing her hue and cry, one Suresh husband of nurse Shiny and her sister Annapurna and Ravishankar came running towards her. The said person who snatched the golden chain by crossing the compound ran away. He was having a height of 5 ft. and was of black colour wearing blue Jeans pant and mixed black colour lining T-shirt. She can identify him. Including the pendent, the said gold ornament was weighing 14.800 grams worth Rs.25,000/-. With these allegations, a complaint came to be filed which was registered in Crime No.105/2011 of town police station, Chikkamagalur, for the offence punishable under Section 392 of IPC and FIR was prepared as per Ex.P.7. Thus, criminal law was set in motion. Complaint is at Ex.P.1.

4. During the course of investigation, Investigation Officer visited the scene of offence and prepared the -4- CRL.RP.NO.701/2015 panchanama. During the course of investigation itself, accused was arrested and at his instance, the snatched gold ornament was seized. Subsequently, it was returned to the complainant on identification.
5. It is the case of the prosecution that when accused was arrested, he gave his voluntary statement as per Ex.P.6 and based upon that, the said gold ornament was seized from his possession.

6. After completion of the investigation, the Investigation Officer has filed the charge-sheet against the accused for the aforesaid offence. Accused was produced before the Court and he was remanded to judicial custody. He was enlarged on bail subsequently.

7. After filing charge-sheet, the learned trial Court took cognizance of the offence, framed the charge against the accused for the offence punishable under Section 392 of IPC read over and explained to him in Kannada i.e., the language known to him. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
8. The prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused, examined 13 witnesses i.e., PWs-1 to 13, got marked documents Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8 and closed prosecution evidence.

9. Thereafter, accused was questioned under Section 313 Cr.P.C. so as to enable him to answer the incriminating circumstances appearing in the evidence of the prosecution. He denied his complicity in the crime. Did not chose to adduce any defence evidence on his behalf.

10. The learned trial Court after hearing the arguments and on perusal of the records, found the accused guilty for the offence punishable under Section 392 of IPC and sentenced him to undergo rigorous imprisonment for two years and fine of Rs.5,000/- with default sentence.

11. This judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Prl. Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Chikkamagalur, was challenged by the accused by -6- CRL.RP.NO.701/2015 preferring an appeal in Crl.A.No.418/2013 before the Prl. Sessions Judge, Chikkamagalur. The first Appellate Court by judgment dated 09.01.2015 confirmed the judgment of conviction and sentence passed against the accused by the trial Court. This is how the revision petitioner is before this Court challenging both the judgments of the Courts below.
12. Heard the arguments of both sides.
Submissions of learned counsel for accused/revision petitioner:

13. It is submitted that in this case recovery panchas have been turned hostile. The very arrest of the accused person by the police is doubtful. There is material contradiction with regard to the arrest of the accused in the evidence of the police witnesses. If evidence of one police officer is accepted, the evidence of other police witness cannot be believed. He submits that accused is a innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this case. In support of his submission, he relies upon various evidence spoken to by the witnesses and also the -7- CRL.RP.NO.701/2015 contradictions, omissions with inconsistencies in the evidence of the prosecution witnesses. He prays to allow the revision petition and acquit the accused for the aforesaid offence.
Submission of learned Addl. SPP

14. With all vehemence, the learned Addl. SPP submits that both the Courts have found accused guilty and it is a heinous offence against complainant in particular and Society in general. From the possession of the accused itself, the said gold ornament was seized being worn by the complainant at the time of alleged snatching. The evidence of the complainant and other witnesses do demonstrate about the involvement of the accused in the commission of the crime. This Court being the revisional Court cannot lightly interfere into the judgment of the trial Court and Appellate Court unless there is illegality and perversity. He prays to dismiss the revision petition.

15. Having considered the arguments of both the side, and on perusal of the records of this case, now we have to ascertain that was there any illegality or perversity committed by both the Courts below in finding the accused guilty or otherwise.

16. It is a case of robbery alleged by the prosecution. So far as robbery is concerned, it is defined under Section 390 of IPC. In all robbery, there is either theft or extortion. Theft is "robbery", if, in order to the committing of the theft, or in committing the theft, or in carrying away or attempting to carry away property obtained by the theft, the offender, for that end, voluntarily causes or attempts to cause to any person death or hurt or wrongful restraint, or fear of instant death or of instant hurt, or of instant wrongful restraint. Extortion is "robbery" if the offender, at the time of committing the extortion, is in the presence of the person put in fear, and commits the extortion by putting that person in fear of instant death, of instant hurt, or of instant wrongful restraint to that person or to some other -9- CRL.RP.NO.701/2015 person, and, by so putting in fear, induces the person so put in fear then and there to deliver up the thing extorted.
17. Section 390 of IPC speaks of punishment for robbery.

18. Thus, it is bounden duty of prosecution to prove the aforesaid ingredients of robbery. In this case, Ex.P.1 is pressed into service by the complainant to show that on 18.05.2011, at about 7.35 p.m., when she was returning to her residential quarters, in the District Hospital compound, near the residential quarters of Shalini and Gracy, the nurses of the said hospital, a person aged in between 25 and 30 years followed her, snatched her gold chain put in her neck with pendant weighing 14.800 grams worth Rs.25,000/- at that time. The said incident took place as per the complainant at about 7.35 p.m. on 18.11.2011. She lodged a complaint at 9 p.m. before the town police station, Chikkamagalur. Thereafter, the police visited the scene of offence on 19.05.2011 and prepared the panchanama as per Ex.P.2 in the presence of panchas. - 10 - CRL.RP.NO.701/2015

19. PW-1 being the complainant, has spoken in line with the contents of the complaint. For the first time, she speaks in her evidence that because of snatching, it cut and a dollar remained with her. She tried to chase him but could not caught hold him. According to her evidence, at that time, her sister Annapurna was accompanying her. In her complaint, she has stated that after the incident of robbery took place, she bombarded and at that time, her sister Annapurna and others came running to her. By that time, the person who robbed the gold chain ran away.

20. She further speaks in her evidence that with regard to said robbery, she lodged a complaint as per Ex.P.1. After 3-4 days of filing complaint, police called her to police station stating that they have arrested the accused. There they showed the accused who was present before the Court on that day and stated that he is the person who committed the robbery. The accused produced the said gold chain.

21. In the cross-examination, she states that on that day at about 7.30 p.m. her sister was standing - 11 - CRL.RP.NO.701/2015 outside the emergency ward. The incident took place at about 7.30 p.m. From the hospital, her quarters was about 200 - 300 ft. away. In between the hospital and quarters, there exists a road running from Chikkamagalur to Hassan. By the side of the road, there is a compound having a good height of about 8 ft. to 10 ft. She further states that at the time of incident, no person was moving on the said road, but the vehicles were moving on the road situated by the side of the hospital compound. According to her, accused came from her behind and it was about 7.30 p.m. It was darkness at that time. Accused snatched her golden chain and ran way from behind and she has seen him. The scene of offence is about 10 - 15 ft. away from the compound. After she did hue and cry, within 5 - 10 minutes CWs-8 and 9 came there. She has denied all the suggestions directed to her.

22. PW-2 Dr.G.Nagaraj, was a pancha to scene of offence - Ex.P.2. He speaks with regard to his presence at the time of conducting the panchanama and he putting signature on the same. Except the denial, nothing is - 12 - CRL.RP.NO.701/2015 elicited from the mouth of this witness so as to disbelieve his evidence spoken in his examination-in-chief. Thus, from the evidence of PWs-1 and 2 coupled with the other evidence placed on record, it is proved that there was a robbery of gold chain worn by complainant on 18.05.2011 at 7.35 p.m.

23. PW-3 Annapurna C. K. being the sister of the complainant speaks that on that day herself and her sister complainant were moving towards their residential quarters about 7.35 p.m. near the residential quarters of Gracy and Shalini. At that time, one person came from behind and robbed the golden chain from the neck of complainant and ran away. Both bombarded as 'thief- thief'. At that time, one Ravishankar came there. Though they tried to catch hold him, he ran away. In her cross- examination, she states that before snatching the golden chain, she has not seen the accused and once, he started running after snatching golden chain, she turned and saw the accused and at that time he was 3 ft. away from her. She admits that near Azad park and post office, the traffic - 13 - CRL.RP.NO.701/2015 police were doing their duty at that time. They went to police station at about 8 p.m. PW-1 lodged the complaint. Thus, evidence of PW-3 also supports with regard to the robbery of gold chain worn by complainant. When the person was running in the darkness, was it possible for these PWs-1 and 3 to identify the accused as the person who committed the robbery has to be explained by the prosecution. PW-1 states that when she went to police station after 3-4 days, she saw the person who was shown as accused who committed the robbery. Then, she identified the accused as the person who committed robbery on her. It is not the case of the prosecution that the street lights or other lights were burning and they could very well identify the person. No such evidence has been brought on record from the mouth of these witnesses.

24. PWs-4 and 5 - Prasad and Raghavendra having cited as seizure panch witnesses to ExP.3. both have been turned as hostile. PW-6 Suresh was the person who reached the complainant and PW-3 when the said incident - 14 - CRL.RP.NO.701/2015 took place. According to the case of prosecution, he also chased accused but PW-6 evidence is silent to that effect. He too has been declared as hostile witness. Nothing worth is elicited from the mouth of PWs-4, 5 and 6 so as to disbelieve their version given in the examination-in- chief. Evidence of PW-6 can be accepted to the extent that he went to the scene of offence after parking his car and the people gathered there told him that there was robbery of gold chain belonging to complainant.

25. PW-7 - Ravishankar S. has come before the trial Court and deposed that on 22.07.2011, when he was in the house he heard the bombardment near his house. He came out of the house and noticed the presence of CW-1/complainant and at that time, it was told to him that her golden chain was robbed by the accused and people were chasing him and he also chased him. The people so chased him caught hold the accused and were bringing him. Police also came there. The police took him in a jeep. CW-1/complainant was searching her dollar in the said place and after search, she could get the pendant. If - 15 - CRL.RP.NO.701/2015 the evidence of PW-7 is compared with the evidence of PWs-1 and 3, altogether different evidence has been spoken to by this PW-7. As per the evidence of PW-1, the incident took place at about 7.35 p.m. but PW-7 says that on 22.07.2011, accused was caught hold by the people who committed the robbery of a gold chain belonging to complainant and he was handed over to the police by the people.

26. It is stated by PW-7 in his cross-examination, on hearing the bombardment he came out of the house along with his wife and the male persons who gathered there, chased the accused. But, he ran away towards the post office. He saw the accused when he was running away. Accused was wearing black coloured jeans pant and black coloured T-shirt. Thereafter, he spoke to the accused in the police station. Police have not recorded his statement. Himself and other persons accompanying him lodged the complaint. Thus, even in the cross- examination also, he has given a quite contradictory evidence with that of PW-1 and PW-3.

27. PW-8 Shalini was a staff nurse and according to her, about 8 months' prior to giving her evidence at 7.30 p.m. she heard the sound of 'thief-thief'. When she came out, nobody was there. She has been declared as hostile witness. Nothing worth is elicited in her cross- examination.

28. PW-9 Dhanpal Naik was the police constable attached to Chikkamagalur town police station at the relevant time. As per his evidence, on 18.05.2011, he was deputed for traffic duties at P.O. Circle and Belur Circle. At 7.30 p.m., towards Azad park from P.O. circle, when he was so moving, one Dr. Uma i.e., PW-1 by opening the compound gate went inside the house and she was followed by woman constable Gehnoza. She heard the noise of Dr. Uma and at that time, when he went inside and enquired, Dr. Uma told him that one person ran away with gold chain towards P.O. Circle, therefore he chased him. He was followed by the said woman constable and Ravi Shankar. The person who was running was wearing blue jeans pant and white T-shirt. He was a - 17 - CRL.RP.NO.701/2015 short person. He ran away towards Mayur hotel. He advised her/PW-1 to lodge a complaint. If the evidence of PW-9 is compared with the evidence of other witnesses discussed supra, this PW-9 has given quite contradictory evidence to that of the evidence of PWs-1, 3 and PW-7.

29. PW-10, Vijay Kumar was goldsmith by profession and he has examined the said gold chain. He certified that it is a gold chain marked as MO.1 and it was half cut. Either PW-1 or PW-3 or any witnesses have not spoken that the said golden chain was really half cut. Evidence of PW-10 is quite contrary to the evidence of PWs-1 and 3.

30. PW-11 - K.T. Gehnoza was the woman head constable. She states that herself and PW-10 were deputed for traffic duties on 18.05.2011 at 7.30 p.m. On that day, both were deputed for searching and apprehending accused in Cr.No.105/2011 i.e., the present crime. AS per the case of prosecution, the said incident of robbery has taken place at 7.30 p.m. on 18.05.2011 but as per the evidence of PW-11 in Cr.No.105/2011 they - 18 - CRL.RP.NO.701/2015 were deputed for searching and apprehending the accused. The said Cr.No.105/2011 was registered based upon the complaint filed by PW-1 at 9 p.m on 18.05.2011. Thus, the evidence of PW-11 is against the content of Ex.P.1 complaint.

31. She further has stated in her cross-examination that on that day she was on bando-bast duty near Kalamandira and at that time, she noticed running away of accused from Azad park toward the labour ward. Herself and PW-10, caught hold the accused. When she caught hold accused was holding golden chain in his hand. Thus, evidence of PW-11 also appears to be contradictory in nature to that of the fact brought on record by the prosecution.

32. PW-12 S. Vijay Prasad, being the Investigation Officer states that he took up the investigation on 19.05.2011 and on 25.02.2011, PWs-9 and 11 produced accused before him. He arrested him and recorded his voluntary statement. PWs-9 and 11 never say that they apprehended the accused on 25.02.2011. As per the - 19 - CRL.RP.NO.701/2015 evidence of this PW-12, in view of the voluntarily statement of accused in the presence of panchas, he seized the said golden chain. The panchas were Prasad and Raghavendra who were examined as PWs-4 and 5. But, PWs-4 and 5 have been turned as hostile. It has come in the evidence of PW-12 that after 4 days of the incident, on 22.05.2011 he arrested accused. Thus, the evidence of PW-12 is quite contrary to the evidence of his own official witnesses i.e., PWs-9 and 11.

33. PW-13 Ravi was the PSI who received the complaint from PW-1 on 18.05.2011. As per his evidence, at 11 p.m. when he was in the police station, Dr.C.K.Uma came to the police station and lodged the complaint as per Ex.P.1. Based upon that he registered the crime in Cr.No.105/2011 and he conducted part of investigation.

34. Thus, on perusal of the evidence of all these witnesses, we find contradictory evidence in the evidence of complainant - Dr.Uma, her sister Annapurna and also with regard to the seizure of the gold ornament i.e. police officers.

35. As per the voluntary statement Ex.P.6, accused was the resident of Kombugatti, Mallenahalli post. As he was addicted to bad vices of drinking alcohol and smoking, and thereafter, he hatched plan to commit robbery or theft. He committed the robbery and he was caught hold by the police. As per his statement, after committing robbery, he went to his village and thereafter, he came to Chikkamagalur. The police officials have not at all stated anything with regard to the contents of this voluntary statement. Thus, the police witnesses themselves have given a clear go bye to the contents of Ex.P.6. Thus, in this case, if the ingredients of robbery are applied, no doubt there was a robbery of the gold chain of the complainant and her chain was snatched away by some person. To that effect, she lodged a complaint. From the evidence of other witnesses, it is not very much clear that it was accused and accused only who committed the robbery. After his arrest, no steps were taken by the Investigation Officer to conduct identification parade so as - 21 - CRL.RP.NO.701/2015 to get identified the accused as the real culprit. Such an evidence is lacking in this case.

36. It is settled principle in criminal jurisprudence that, it is the duty of the prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt to the hilt. Even if a slightest doubt arises in the case of prosecution, by proving the chain of circumstances with regard to the commission of the offence, then only the accused can be held to be guilty. But, in this case, we find material contradictions, omissions, inconsistencies and discrepancies in the evidence of the prosecution witnesses which have not been properly explained by the prosecution. The learned trial court and the first Appellate Court though had sufficient material showing the aforesaid lacuna in the case of the prosecution, but have hurriedly believed the evidence of complainant - PW-1, her sister Annapurna - PW-3 and the evidence of the Investigation Officers and found the accused guilty which is improper. Therefore, we find that both trial Court and the first Appellate Court have not properly appreciated the - 22 - CRL.RP.NO.701/2015 evidence placed on record and have wrongly held the accused guilty which is incorrect. Therefore, the interference is very much required in this revision by this Court with regard to the perversity and illegality committed by the trial Court in finding the accused guilty. Consequentially, it is held that accused is not guilty of the offence punishable under Section 392 of IPC and he has to be acquitted by giving benefit of doubt.
37. In view of my foregoing discussion, the revision petition succeeds and deserves to be allowed. Resultantly, I pass the following:
(i) Revision petition filed by the revision petitioner/accused under Section 397 read with Section 401 of Cr.P.C. is allowed.

The judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed in C.C.No.614/2011 dated 18.11.2013 by the Prl. Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Chikkamagalur and confirmed in Crl.A.No.418/2013 dated 09.01.2015 by the Prl. - 23 - CRL.RP.NO.701/2015 Sessions Judge, Chikkamagalur, are hereby set aside.
(ii) Accused is acquitted of the charge punishable under Section 392 of IPC. His bail bonds stands cancelled. He is set at liberty.
(iii) Fine amount if paid by the accused shall be refunded to him digitally after collecting necessary document by the trial Court, forthwith.
(iv) Office to send the copy of this order to both the Courts below for reference along with trial Court records as well as Sessions Court records forthwith.

case_name: Sri Manoj Kumar v. State By Jeevan Bheema

paragraphs.text: These appeals are filed by appellants-accused Nos.1 to 8 and 10 under Section 374(2) of Cr.P.C. for setting aside the judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the LVI Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bangalore in S.C.Nos.158/2010 clubbed with S.C.547/2011 for having found the appellants guilty and convicted for the offences punishable under 7 Sections 120B , 364A , 395 , 397 read with Section 149 of IPC.
2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellants and learned High Court Government Pleader for the State.
3. The appellants are accused and respondent is the complainant-State, the rank of the parties before the Trial Court is retained for the sake of convenience.

4. The Assistant Commissioner of Police, Halasuru Sub-Division filed the charge sheet against the appellant-accused persons alleging that the complainant-CW.1/P.W.3 being the Branch Manager of Muthoot Mini Nidhi Finance, situated at No.120, 1st floor, Alfa Diamond Plaza, New Thippasandra Road, Bangalore that on 02.06.2009, in the evening at 5.30 8 p.m., after locking the strong room and the main door, while he was returning to his house in his Honda Activa scooter bearing No.KA-03-EK-3890 by keeping the office keys in the dickey of the said scooter, when he was proceeding near Indira Nagar, accused Nos.6 and 9 followed him in a motor bike bearing No.KA-02- ED-15 and dashed to the vehicle of CW.1, due to which, he fell down. At that time, accused Nos.3, 7 and 8 came in a white colour Maruthi Omni van bearing No.KA-03-M-8138 and abducted the CW.1 to Malur Road under the guise of providing treatment. Accused No.7 poured the spirit on the face of CW.1 in the said Omni van. Accused Nos.3 and 7 assaulted the complainant-CW.1, by threatening him forcibly took the cash of Rs.20,000/- and snatched the mobile phone from him, then pushed out CW.1 from the Omni Van. Thereafter, the accused went near the scooter of the complainant where he was lying, took 9 the keys of Muthoot Mini Nidhi Finance from the scooter and also strong room keys from the dickey of the said scooter. Then accused Nos.1 to 10 assembled and then went to the Muthoot Finance office, opened the main door and committed the dacoity of golden ornaments weighing 40kg and 490 grams worth of Rs.5,68,40,000/- and escaped from the spot. During the investigation, the police arrested the accused persons. The case against accused No.9 was split up, he died during the trial. Accused No.10 was later arrested and a separate charge sheet has been filed in S.C.No.547/2011 and accused Nos.1 to 8 were tried in S.C.No.158/2010. The charges were framed, they denied the charges and claimed to be tried. Accordingly, the prosecution examined 42 witnesses as per PWs.1 to 42, got marked 74 documents as per Exs.P.1 to 74 and 42 material objects as per M.O.Nos.1 to 42. After closing the evidence, the 10 statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded. The case of the accused is one of the total denial, but not examined any witnesses except marking Ex.D.1.
5. After hearing the arguments, the Trial Court found the appellants guilty and convicted as under:
(i) Accused Nos.1 to 8 and 10 are sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 1 one year and to pay fine of Rs.5,000/- each for the offence punishable under Section 120B of IPC.
(ii) They also sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 9 years and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/- each for the offence punishable under Section 364(A) of IPC.
(iii) They also sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 9 years and to pay fine 11 of Rs.10,000/- each for the offence punishable under Section 395 of IPC.

(iv) They also sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 5 years for the offence punishable under Section 397 of IPC and in default of payment of fine, they shall undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 1 year. All the sentences are ordered to run concurrently.
6. Being aggrieved with the judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the Trial Court, the accused Nos.1 to 8 and 10 are before this Court by filing these appeals.

7. Sri T. Prakash, the learned counsel for the appellants appearing for accused Nos.1, 3, 8 and 10 has contended that the judgment of the Trial Court is erroneous and illegal. The Trial Court has not 12 considered that there was delay in lodging the complaint as the incident said to be took place on 02.06.2009 at 5.30 p.m., but the complaint was filed at 8.00 p.m., on the very next day. But the FIR was reached the Magistrate on 04.06.2009. The Investigating Officer investigated the matter and registered the FIR against three unknown persons. The version of the PW.1 is not believable since after the incident, he went and stayed in his relative's house without lodging any complaint and intimating to any persons which is unnatural conduct and even he has not intimated to his employers. He further contended that the complainant said to be took treatment in Vaidehi Hospital, but no documents produced and the material objects also not produced before the Court except marking the photos without any certificates. The Maruti Van is said to be used for commission of offence was also not proved. The 13 witnesses have turned hostile. All the prosecution witnesses including the panch witnesses turned hostile, not supported the prosecution case. The fingerprint which was said to be taken also not produced before the Court. The CCTV Camera Footage kept in the Muthoot Finance is not produced. There is no evidence regarding robbery or dacoity. The abduction or kidnapping also not proved. The T.I.P. has been conducted by the Tahsildar. The ASI is said to be identified the assailants, but the T.I.P. report not produced, therefore, it has no value. The complainant failed to identify the assailants. The Investigating Officer relied upon the Newspaper cutting regarding seizure of the golden ornaments which is marked as Ex.D.1 and the date of arrest was shown as 09.06.2009 and 10.06.2009, but the properties were seized on 08.06.3009 itself. The complainant claimed the insurance for theft of materials which shows this 14 case was set up in order to claim the insurance amount.

8. The learned counsel further contended that the accused No.10 was arrested after one and half year of the incident. Nothing has been recovered from him. None of the witnesses supported the prosecution case. There is zero evidence against accused No.10.

9. The learned counsel further contended that there was two keys for the safe locker, one key with the complainant and another key with the Assistant Manager. The same was noted in the Register in Ex.P.50. But the office was opened and removed the ornaments without breaking the lock which falsify the case of the prosecution. The complaint was drafted by the Director of the Muthoot Finance but not by the complainant. The case was based upon the 15 circumstantial evidence, but none of the witnesses have supported the prosecution case. Hence, prayed for allowing the appeals.

10. Sri Vishnumurthy, learned counsel for the appellants-accused Nos.2, 4, 6 and 7 has adopted the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant Sri.T.Prakash and further contended that in the evidence of PW.3, he has to identify accused No.3, but he has identified accused No.4 in the Court, there is no corroboration with the evidence of PW.7 and the T.I.P. conducted. PW.7 should identify accused No.1 but the witness already identified the accused in the Police Station, but PW.7 has wrongly identified accused No.7. As per the evidence of PW.3, accused No.1 was on the spot, but as per the evidence of PW.7, accused No.1 was in the vehicle, there is a contradiction in their evidence. PW.3 was unable to 16 identify the accused who had kidnapped him from the spot. PW.3 stayed in the house of PW.23 after the incident. He went to the hospital, but he has not disclosed to PW.23 to his employer and he has stated that both keys are with him, but not explained as to why those keys were kept with him. As per the rules, one key must be with the Assistant Manager. The T.I.P. conducted by the PW.7 has stated only in question and answer but not produced and marked the proceedings for having identified the accused. None of the mahazar witnesses supported the case of the prosecution except police officials. The recoveries were not produced and not identified by any of the panch witnesses. The conduct of the appellant is very much surprised as he has not disclosed the incident to any persons. Therefore, the story of the prosecution is doubtful. The benefit of doubt shall be extended to the accused. Hence, prayed for allowing the appeals. 17

11. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader supported the judgment of the Trial Court and contended that the injured took treatment in the hospital, therefore, he has not lodged the complaint. PWs.1 to 8 have supported the prosecution case. T.I.P. was conducted and the witnesses are identified the accused. Therefore, prayed for dismissing the appeals.
12. The points that arise for my consideration are:

dashed the complainant to his scooter and abducted him in a Omni Van, robbed cash of Rs.20,000/- and mobile phone, then committed dacoity by removing 40 kgs 950 grams of gold ornaments from the 18 Muthoot Finance, thereby committed the offence punishable under Sections 120B , 364(A) , 397 , 395 read with Section 149 of IPC?
2) Whether the judgment of the Trial Court calls for the interference?"

13. Having heard the arguments and on perusal of the records, prior to appreciation of the evidence, it is worth to have a cursory look on the evidence adduced by the prosecution before the Trial Court.

14. PW.1-Sajeev who is the spot panch witness to the Ex.P.1 and seizure panch witness to the Ex.P.2 for the seizure of M.Os.1 to 40. He has deposed that the Police called him to the Muthoot Finance Premises and prepared the panchanama as per Ex.P.1. They also deposed that the Police seized M.Os.1 and 2- Godrej Lock. M.O.3-black rexin bag, M.O.4-bottle with 19 chemical. The axa blade, fine cutter, grew cutter, hand gloves kept in the rexin bag and the same were seized by the Police under the panchanama. In the cross examination, he has stated that he cannot say any description of the property that when he went to the spot, the police already were in the spot, 50 to 100 people were assembled. The properties were already collected from the shop. He further admits that the police never called to the Police station and he is not aware about the contents of the panchanamas. He further submits that the police informed him that there was dacoity committed, but he is not aware about the same. On perusal of the evidence of this witness, except for spot panchanama said to be conducted by the police, his evidence is not useful to the prosecution case 20

15. PW.2-Raju Ram, the another panch witness to Ex.P.3 for seizure of gold articles and according to his evidence, he is a jeweler, on 10.06.2009, the Hennur Police called him for weighing the golden ornaments. He was taken to Hosakote Taluk. A person came in the vehicle and he has identified the said person as accused No.3 and he has stated his name is Jayakumar. Then, the said Jayakumar shown some gold items which was hidden in the ground which was seized by the police under Ex.P.3 and further submits he cannot identify the golden ornaments seized by the police by looking to the photographs. He has treated as hostile and he denied the suggestion made by the learned P.P. and once again, he identified accused No.2 as Jayakumar and he has denied the photographs showing the golden ornaments. Though he has denied that he has stated before the police that he will identify the golden ornaments, but 21 deposed false. He further denies Ex.P.4 statement made to the police. In the cross examination of the learned counsel for the accused, he has stated that the police came to the shop for weighing the golden ornaments and he cannot say exactly who were the persons present in the car. The police themselves dug the floor and took the bag and he further admits he is not aware about the sealing of the bag. Except weighing the golden ornaments, he do not know anything and he further admits that he has identified accused No.2 only on the say of the police. On careful perusal of the evidence of this witness, though this witness taken to the spot for recovery and weighing the golden ornaments, but he has turned hostile not fully supported the case of the prosecution and he has identified accused No.3 instead of accused No.2 and later he has changed his version and stated that the police told him to identify accused No.2 and he is not 22 aware about the case and denied Ex.P.4. Therefore, his evidence is not consistent to believe and of no worth.

16. PW.3-Isac John who is the complainant and a star witness to this case. He has deposed that he is worked in the Muthoot finance as Manager from 1999 till 02.06.2009 and the said company running the finance by receiving the golden ornaments. On the date of incident i.e. on 02.06.2009, at 5.30 p.m., he closed the office, went in his motorcycle KA 03 EK 3890 when he was proceeding near the Corporation Bank main road, Indiranagar, a scooter dashed to him, he fell down, sustained injury on the face as well as knee chip. About 8 to 10 persons were present over there, one person opened the dickey of his scooter, took the bank key and 2 to 3 persons came in a Maruti Van and asked to come to the hospital, then, 23 he sat in the car, one person assaulted and robbed Rs.20,000/- from him by spreading the chemical on his face then at 9.30 p.m., the car went towards the Hosakote to Malur. Then he was pushed out and went away. A watchman came there, provided some water thereafter, he telephoned to one Vargeese Kurian and he went to the Vaidehi hospital, after obtaining the treatment, he went to the house of his relative at 1.30 a.m. and in the morning, he went to the spot, the scooter was not found, then he telephoned to the Bank Director, thereafter, he came to the office at Thippasandra and found the strong room was open, then he came to know about missing of 40 kg 650 grams of gold worth of more than Rs.5.00 crores and he found rod, axa blade, chemical bottle, gloves, monkey cap etc. then the police shifted him to the hospital and obtained the complaint as per Ex.P.5. He identified Ex.P.1 panchanama and M.Os.1 to 40 are 24 the materials seized from the spot. His evidence will be appreciated in the later part of the judgment.

17. PW.4-S.G.Kulakarni is the Regional Manager of Muthoot Finance. He has deposed that on 03.06.2009, he received phone call from the Director Mathews to come to the branch office, he went there, the office was open, the articles were scattered, the police not allowed him to go inside. He further deposes that on 06.06.2009, the J.B.Nagar Police called him and obtained signature on Ex.P.6 and informed that some articles seized from the Police. He saw the articles in a bag. He further says the police took to the house of accused No.1 and shown the articles to him and he further deposes that he cannot identify the golden ornaments.

18. The public prosecutor treated this witness as hostile and this witness has stated that he cannot 25 say that the accused No.1 was in the Police Station or not. The police asked him to come along with them, hence he went there and he says accused No.1 shown the rexin bag containing the golden ornaments. In the cross examination, this witness has stated that there was two keys for the room, one key with the Assistant Manager and another key with the Manager and in order to open the strong room, both should come and open the door by unlocking the same. He further deposes that there was CCTV camera and siren installed in the office and if any person entered the strong room, the siren will ring and if any other key is used to put on the lock it will not open and further deposes, there was an insurance coverage for the articles. He further deposes that the said building is consisting for four flours, their office is situated in the ground flour, there are houses and shops in the upstairs and if anybody goes by staircase, it will be 26 noticed by the people of the houses residing in the said building. A suggestion was made by the learned counsel for the accused that when they are not able to obtain the insurance claim, they filed the complaint.

19. On perusal of the evidence of this witness, it reveals, though he is a panch witness to the Ex.P.6 for seizure of articles at the instance of accused No.1, but those articles were not produced and marked before the Court. The CCTV was installed in the office, the footage was not collected by the Investigating Officer and produced before the Court. If any person goes inside the strong room by using the any other key, the siren will ring, but no such siren was heard by the other persons residing in the same building. As per his evidence, if any person entered the building through staircase, the other inmates of the house will be noticed. But no such person stated before the court 27 about the arrival of the accused or entering to the Muthoot finance by opening the main door and strong room for the best reasons known to the Investigating Officer and this witness why the CCTV footage not collected and produce before the Court, that will clinch the issue and easy for identification. Therefore, his evidence is not believable without corroboration of the any independent witnesses.
20. PW.5-Nemaram who is the panch witness to the Ex.P.8 seizure of golden articles, he has turned hostile not supported the prosecution case. That apart, he is a stock witness to the police.

21. PW.6-Srinivasa Murthy, an Accountant of Muthoot Finance, he deposes that as on the date of complaint, he was present and on the earlier day i.e., on 02.06.2009, they closed the office, went to the house and on the very next day, when he came to the 28 office, he found the office was opened, somebody stolen the articles from the strong room, then the police came to the spot. He further deposes that on 05.06.2009, he went to the Police Station and again on 10.06.2009 he was called to the Police Station and police told they seized the articles and they shown 9 persons were arrested. Again on 28.06.2009, they informed the articles were seized. In the cross examination, he has stated that in the said branch they have permitted to keep only 5 lakhs worth of golden ornaments and in order to keep more ornaments, they have to obtain permission from the main branch and the main branch is permitted to keep only golden ornaments worth of 30 to 40 lakhs. He also confirmed there was two keys for the strong room one key with the Assistant Manager and another key with the Manager and in order to open the strong room, both keys namely B1 and B2 are required. He 29 further admitted there was a register maintained in the office mentioning the holder of the keys and the said keys were kept by only Manager and the Assistant Manager, but not any other persons. He further admits, on the next day when he came to the office, the Police were present and came to know about the theft. He further admits there were other houses and shops situated in the same building, CCTV camera also installed.

22. PW.7-Girithimmappa, ASI who deposes that on 02.06.2009 at about 5.30 p.m., he received phone call from the control room that there was an accident on the Indiranagar Main road, he went to the spot, he found Hoysala vehicle also arrived on the spot, there were two, two wheelers found on the spot, one is Honda Activa and another is Yamaha crux. Some public told him that three persons came in a 30 van and took the scooter raider, then he has informed to the tiger van, one person was present on the spot and told the rider of the Honda Activa was his uncle and there was treatment in the Hosmat Hospital. Hence, he requested the vehicle but he refused to give the vehicle. He further deposes that later the vehicles were seized by the Jeevan Bhimanagar police under panchamnama Ex.P10. Exs.P.11 to P.13 are the photographs of the vehicle. He further deposes that on 24.06.2009, the police took him to the Bengaluru jail, conducted T.I.P. and he has identified accused No.1 was the accused before the Court. In the cross examination, he has stated that he do not know how the accident was occurred, there were 10 to 15 people present on the spot. The Hoysala van was on the spot, two police officials were there in the said car and he further admitted he has not reported to the Police Station regarding vehicle and request made by the 31 person for the vehicle and he further admitted, he came to know from the J.B. Nagar Police that accused were traced. Then he went to the Police station, saw the accused in the J.B. Nagar Police station. He further admits he has identified the accused No.1 as told by the Police Officers. He further admits he has not stated the description of the accused before the J.B.Nagar police. He further admits, he do not know when the panchanama was prepared for seizing of the motor cycle and Honda Activa. This witness is very important witness to the prosecution, he has said to be seen accused No.1 on the spot along with the other public, but, he has seen accused No.1 in J.B. Nagar police Station and identified him as accused No.1 and on the say of the J.B.Nagar police, he identified the accused No.1 and when the police shown the accused No.1 in the Police station, subsequently, he said to be identified in the jail. Therefore, T.I.P. conducted by 32 the Tahsildar-PW.37 and identifying accused No.1 by this witness is not in accordance with law and not believable and the identification of the accused No.1 by this witness is only empty formality and it has no evidentiary value.

23. PW.8-T Raju, ASI, who arrested accused No.9 and seized the golden articles deposes that one person found with bag, he apprehended him and his name was Suresh (accused No.9) who is absconding and on perusal of the bag, he was in possession of 1,562 grams golden ornaments, he prepared the panchanama Ex.P.15. Though the learned counsel for the accused cross examined this witness, but accused No.9 was absconding and no judgment was delivered against accused No.9 and he was reported dead.

24. PW.9-Jayaram, who is panch witness to Ex.P8 seizure of golden articles from accused No.8. 33 This witness turned hostile not supported the prosecution case. Hence, his evidence is not useful to the prosecution case.
25. PW.10-Yashwanth Raj Jain, another panch witness to the Ex.P.16 seizure of the golden articles from accused No.6, he also turned hostile and not supported the prosecution case.
26. PW.11-Mallesh, panch witness to Ex.P.17 for seizure of golden articles from accused No.5, he also turned hostile and not supported the prosecution case.
27. PW.12-Devaraj, another panch witness to the Ex.P.17, seizure of golden articles from accused No.5, he also turned hostile, not supported the prosecution case.
28. PW.13-Noorulla, panch witness to Ex.P.19 seizure of articles from accused No.3, turned hostile and not supported the prosecution case.
29. PW.14-Chinnaswamy, seizure of articles from accused No.4 under Ex.P.20, he also turned hostile and not supported the case.
30. PW.15-M. Ravi Kumar, panch witness to Ex.P.16, seizure of articles from accused No.6, he also turned hostile and not supported the case.
31. PW.16-Pradeep Kumar, the land lord who let out a shop to the accused, but he has turned hostile, not supported the prosecution case.
32. PW.17-Raghu @ Rukmangada is the owner of the apartment staying in the same building, turned hostile and not supported the case.
33. PW.18-R.Srinivasa, panch witness to the Ex.P.24 seizure of two wheelers, he also turned hostile.
34. PW.19-Jayaram, seizure panch witness to Ex.P.3 for seizure of golden articles from accused No.2 who has also turned hostile.
35. PW.20-Deepak Kumar, who showed the Maruti van to the accused also turned hostile and not supported the case.
36. PW.21-Jabiulla, who is the panch witness to Ex.P.24 seizure of two wheelers turned hostile and not supported the case.
37. PW.22-Abdul Salim, panch witness to the Ex.P.24, he also turned hostile and not supported the case.

38. PW.23-Vergees Kurian, who has deposed that about 7 years back he came to know that CW.1 was unconscious, therefore, he went to Chikkathirupati, he brought him to the Vaidehi Hospital and he came to know that some unknown persons taken him in a van and left him, he provided treatment and came to know some persons committed theft in the Muthoot Finance. According to his evidence, he has no knowledge about the incident.

39. PW.24-K.S.Mahesh, who arrested the accused No.5 and produced before the Investigating Officer and then the accused took the police official and witness to the house and police seized golden articles under Ex.P.17 but he was unable to identify the accused in the Court. In the cross examination, he has admitted that he do not know the boundaries of the accused house, he do not know the owner of the 37 house and except apprehending the accused, he do not know anything and as per his evidence, though he has apprehended accused No.5, but he was unable to say the details of the recovery under Ex.P.17 and the panch witnesses were already turned hostile and the identity of the articles were not proved before the Court.

40. PW.25-C.P.Madappa PSI, deposed that, on 09.06.2009 at 10.00 p.m., the ASI and other police officials were taken for tracing the accused and one person was found near Byappanahalli and he was apprehended and brought back before the police station and on enquiry, he stated that his name was Nirmalraj and he identified the said person as accused No.1 in the Court. In the cross examination, P.W.25 has stated that for tracing accused No.1, photographs given to him and he has not prepared any 38 panchanama on the spot. No memo was given to him for tracing the accused and for apprehending the accused and he has not given any report to the investigation officer.

41. On perusal of the evidence of P.W.25, it reveals that in order to apprehend the accused, the photographs and descriptions were given to him, and that, if he arrests any person, at least, he should submit a report to the investigation officer. Absolutely, there is no document produced by him or marked by the prosecution to show that this witness was deputed for apprehending accused No.1 and his evidence appears to be an imaginary one and not in accordance with law.

42. P.W.26 - H.G. Vasudev, retired Police Sub Inspector deposed that, on 09.06.2009, he was deputed for apprehending the accused in this case. 39 Then he apprehended accused No.2 and produced before the investigation officer and the investigation officer recorded the voluntary statement of accused No.2 that he participated in the commission of dacoity in Muthoot Finance. In the cross examination, P.W.26 admitted that he has not prepared any report for producing the accused and no description given to him for apprehension of accused No.2. The evidence of this witness appears to be an imaginary and not believable.

43. P.W.27-Munaiah, retired ASI, deposed that on 10.06.2009, he was deputed and apprehended the accused-Manoj Kumar (accused No.4) and produced before the investigation officer. The investigation officer seized the golden ornaments under Ex.P.20. He has stated that the Investigating Officer given photograph to him and therefore, he apprehended 40 accused No.4, but he has not stated in the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. that the investigation officer given the photographs, which reveals that the prosecution tried to develop the evidence after admission given by P.Ws.25 and 26.

44. P.W.28 - M. Venkataramanappa, retired ASI, has deposed that he apprehended accused No.1 on 10.06.2009. According to his evidence, that on the said day at 6.30 p.m., he apprehended accused No.1 and produced before the investigation officer. Then, the investigation officer seized gold articles from him and compared the evidence of P.W.25, who has stated that he apprehended accused No.1 on 09.06.2009, but P.W.28 says that accused No.1 was arrested on 10.06.2009. P.W.25 does not speak about the seizure of gold articles, but P.W.28 deposes that the gold articles seized from accused No.1. There is 41 contradiction between the evidence of P.W.25 and P.W.28 regarding the arrest of accused No.1 and the seizure of articles.
